result: In the quiet hours before sunrise I often think about how time curls back on itself, like steam from a cup of tea spiraling against a pane of cold glass. We pretend clocks are linear rulers, but they are really soft, malleable loops that change length depending on whether we are bored, grieving, exhilarated, or newly in love. Memory clings to those variable stretches, pinning bright fragments like moth
